candidates.change_summary: Change the block assignment from block.number + 1 to block.number + 2, altering when settle becomes callable.
Remove the require(msg.value == 1 ether) check, allowing lockInGuess to be called without sending 1 ether.
Remove the require(guesses[msg.sender].block == 0) check, allowing a user to overwrite a pending guess.
Delete the require that the caller has no existing guess, allowing lockInGuess to be called again before the first guess is settled.
Delete the require that exactly 1 ether is sent, allowing lockInGuess to be called with zero or other payment amounts.
Replace the stored guess hash assignment with a self-assignment, so the supplied hash is ignored.
Replace the guess deadline assignment with block.number, making the guess immediately settleable in the next block.
Change the first require in lockInGuess to require(msg.value == 0), so callers sending 1 ether revert instead of completing.
Change the first require in lockInGuess to require(msg.value == 2 ether), so callers sending exactly 1 ether revert instead of completing.
Change the recorded block to block.number + 2, which makes the first lockInGuess with 1 ether revert on the subsequent settle instead of allowing a normal complete call.
Delete the require that the caller has no existing guess, allowing repeated lockInGuess calls to complete instead of reverting after one guess.
Changed the require on guesses[msg.sender].block from == 0 to != 0, allowing overwrite when a previous guess exists.
Changed the value check from msg.value == 1 ether to msg.value != 1 ether, rejecting exactly 1 ether and allowing other values.
Changed the assignment target from guesses[msg.sender].guess to guesses[msg.sender].block, making the function store the hash in block instead of guess.
Changed the block-number assignment target from guesses[msg.sender].block to guesses[msg.sender].guess, so the lock block is not recorded.
Changed the block assignment from block.number + 1 to block.number, causing settle to be callable in the same block.
Changed the block assignment from block.number + 1 to block.number + 2, delaying when settle can succeed.
Deleted the msg.value == 1 ether requirement, allowing lockInGuess to be called without paying 1 ether.
Deleted the assignment that records the guess hash, leaving only the block number update.
Deleted the assignment that records the block number, leaving guesses[msg.sender].block unchanged at zero.
Moved the msg.value requirement after the state writes, so payment is checked only after the guess is recorded.
Replace the first require condition with a always-true expression, allowing repeated lockInGuess calls by the same sender.
Change the required payment in lockInGuess from exactly 1 ether to at least 1 ether.
Remove the payment requirement in lockInGuess, allowing zero-value calls.
Set the recorded block to the current block number instead of the next block number.
Set the recorded block to block.number + 2 instead of block.number + 1.
Delete the statement that records the guessed hash.
Delete the statement that records the block number.
Swap the order of the two assignment statements in lockInGuess.
Replace the first require in lockInGuess with a no-op require(true), allowing guesses to be overwritten repeatedly.
Replace the first require in lockInGuess with require(guesses[msg.sender].block != 0), requiring a previous non-zero block instead of forbidding it.
Change the deposit requirement from exactly 1 ether to any non-zero value.
Set the stored block to the current block number instead of the next block.
Changed the assignment of the guess block from block.number + 1 to block.number.
Changed the assignment of the guess block from block.number + 1 to block.number + 2.
Removed the assignment that records the guessed hash.
Removed the assignment that records the block number for the guess.
Changed the assignment target from the caller's guess hash to the caller's guess block.
Replaced the assignment to guesses[msg.sender].guess with no-op preserving the hash argument.
Replaced the assignment to guesses[msg.sender].guess with a different value derived from the sender.
Replaced the assignment to guesses[msg.sender].guess with the zero hash.
Replaced the assignment to guesses[msg.sender].block with block.number, making the guess immediately settleable.
Replaced the assignment to guesses[msg.sender].block with block.number + 2, delaying when the guess can be settled.
Replaced the assignment to guesses[msg.sender].block with zero, which makes the stored guess appear unlocked/inactive regardless of the guess being set.
Deleted the assignment to guesses[msg.sender].guess, leaving the stored guess unset.
Deleted the assignment to guesses[msg.sender].block, leaving the guess not active and thus not settleable.
Deleted the msg.value == 1 ether requirement, allowing guesses to be locked without paying.
Moved the guesses[msg.sender].guess assignment after the block assignment, so a caller with nonzero block state may have guess overwritten differently.
Replace the duplicate-guess guard require(guesses[msg.sender].block == 0) with require(true), allowing repeated lockInGuess calls to update the stored guess and block.
Change the duplicate-guess guard to require(guesses[msg.sender].block == block.number), allowing a second lockInGuess in the same block as an expired prior guess.
Change the duplicate-guess guard to require(guesses[msg.sender].block != block.number), allowing repeated guesses unless the prior block was set to the current block.
Change the payment guard to require(msg.value >= 1 ether), allowing larger payments to pass lockInGuess.
Change the payment guard to require(msg.value != 1 ether), requiring any value other than exactly 1 ether.
Store block.number instead of block.number + 1 as the user's guess block.
Store block.number - 1 instead of block.number + 1 as the user's guess block.
Reset the stored guess block to 0 instead of setting it to block.number + 1.
Delete the assignment that records the user's guess hash.
Delete the assignment that records the user's guess block number.
Replace `require(guesses[msg.sender].block == 0);` with `require(guesses[msg.sender].block != 0);` in lockInGuess.
Replace `require(msg.value == 1 ether);` with `require(msg.value != 1 ether);` in lockInGuess.
Replace `guesses[msg.sender].block = block.number + 1;` with `guesses[msg.sender].block = block.number;` in lockInGuess.
Replace `guesses[msg.sender].block = block.number + 1;` with `guesses[msg.sender].block = 1;` in lockInGuess.
Replace `guesses[msg.sender].guess = hash;` with `guesses[msg.sender].guess = bytes32(0);` in lockInGuess.
Replace `guesses[msg.sender].guess = hash;` with `guesses[msg.sender].guess = bytes32(uint256(hash) + 1);` in lockInGuess.
Replace `require(guesses[msg.sender].block == 0);` with `require(true);` in lockInGuess.
Replace `require(msg.value == 1 ether);` with `require(true);` in lockInGuess.
Change the guard so any non-zero block number is rejected instead of only block 0.
Allow the sender to call lockInGuess repeatedly regardless of their previously recorded block.
Require a payment amount other than exactly 1 ether.
Store the caller's current block number instead of the next block number.
Change transfer amount from 2 ether to 0 ether in settle()
Delete the require that block.number > guesses[msg.sender].block
Replace blockhash(guesses[msg.sender].block) with blockhash(block.number) in settle()
Remove the condition 'answer != 0' from the if statement in settle()
Replace 'guesses[msg.sender].guess == answer' with 'guesses[msg.sender].guess != answer' in settle()
Delete the line 'guesses[msg.sender].block = 0;' in settle()
Replace 'block.number > guesses[msg.sender].block' with 'block.number >= guesses[msg.sender].block' in settle()
Weaken the guard on line 26 from block != 0 to block == 0, changing which callers may proceed past the first require in settle().
Weaken the timing guard on line 27 from strictly greater-than to greater-than-or-equal, allowing settle() at the same block as the recorded guess block.
Compute the answer from the current block instead of the stored guess block, changing which hash is used for settlement.
Reset the caller's stored block to the current block number instead of zero, changing the post-settle eligibility state.
Change the payout condition from requiring answer != 0 to requiring answer == 0, altering when a winner is paid.
Change the payout amount from 2 ether to 1 ether, altering the observable value transfer on a successful settle().
Delete the require that the caller has a non-zero guess block, allowing settle() to proceed for accounts that never called lockInGuess.
Replace the strict block-number comparison with a non-strict one, allowing settle() to execute in the same block as the recorded guess.
Replace answer with blockhash(block.number), changing which block hash is checked against the stored guess.
Delete the reset of the caller's guess block to zero, so a successful or failed settle does not clear the recorded guess block.
Replace the conjunctive payout condition with a disjunction, so a caller is paid if either the answer is non-zero or the stored guess matches.
Replace the fixed 2 ether payout with a 1 ether payout, changing the amount transferred on a successful settle.
Delete the require guard `require(block.number > guesses[msg.sender].block);`, allowing settle to proceed before the committed block has passed.
Delete the nonzero blockhash guard `answer != 0` from the if condition, so a zero blockhash can be treated as a winning answer.
Delete the state reset `guesses[msg.sender].block = 0;`, allowing repeated settle attempts after a failed guess.
Move the state reset `guesses[msg.sender].block = 0;` after the external value transfer, changing reentrancy/call-time state visibility.
Replace the payout amount `2 ether` with `1 ether` in the transfer, changing the observable ETH received by a winning caller.
Change the winner payout from transferring 2 ether to transferring 1 ether.
Remove the answer != 0 guard so a successful hash match can still pay out when the blockhash returns zero.
Change the timing check from strictly greater-than to greater-than-or-equal, allowing settlement in the locking block.
Change the locked-guess existence check to compare against 1 instead of 0.
Change the hash source from the stored guess block to the current block.
The settle function now requires the caller's recorded block to be strictly before the current block number, rather than after the recorded block.
The settle function now checks that the recorded block equals the current block number instead of requiring the current block to be past it.
The settle function now computes the answer using the current block number instead of the caller's recorded block number.
The settle function now resets the caller's recorded block to 1 instead of 0, preventing successful callers from locking in a new guess afterward.
The settle function now pays out 1 ether on a correct guess instead of the original 2 ether.
The settle function now requires the answer to be zero before paying out, adding a zero-hash condition to the payout check.
The settle function now resets the caller's recorded block before checking the block-number timing requirement, allowing settlement attempts to clear the guess even when the timing check would fail.
Replace the strict block-number check with >=, allowing settle in the same block as the locked guess.
Replace the nonzero-answer check with a check that answer is zero, inverting the payout condition.
Replace the equality check between the stored guess and the answer with an inequality check.
Change the payout amount from 2 ether to 0 ether.
Delete the assignment that clears the player's active guess block, leaving settlement state intact.
Replace strict block-number check with a non-strict one, allowing settlement in the same block when the guess was locked.
Remove the answer != 0 guard so a zero blockhash can satisfy the payout condition.
Change the payout amount from 2 ether to 1 ether.
Replace the recorded block number with the current block number when computing the answer hash.
Change the equality comparison to an inequality comparison in the payout condition.
Change the answer != 0 guard to answer == 0 so payout only occurs when the hash is zero.
Use the sender's stored guess as the answer source instead of the blockhash.
Delete the payout transfer statement so no funds are ever sent.
Delete the requirement that the guess block is nonzero.
Delete the requirement that the current block number exceeds the recorded guess block.
Changed the settle guard from requiring block.number > guesses[msg.sender].block to requiring block.number >= guesses[msg.sender].block.
Changed the payout amount from 2 ether to 1 ether in settle.
Changed the answer comparison condition from equality to inequality in settle.
Deleted the reset of guesses[msg.sender].block to zero after reading the blockhash in settle.
Replace the requirement that the caller has a nonzero guess block with a requirement that the caller has a zero guess block, preventing valid settle calls from proceeding.
Replace the block-number freshness check so settlement is only allowed before or at the guessed block instead of strictly after it.
Change the random answer source from blockhash of the guessed block to blockhash of the current block.
Remove the answer != 0 guard so a zero blockhash could still lead to a payout if the stored guess is zero.
Change the comparison against the stored guess to a comparison with a fixed zero hash, making successful settlement dependent on a zero answer.
Delete the statement clearing the caller's guess block after settlement, leaving the stored block number unchanged.
Delete the payout transfer statement so a successful guess never sends ether.
Replace the strict block-number check with a non-strict comparison, allowing settle() in the same block as the recorded guess block.
Remove the requirement that the caller's guess block is nonzero, allowing settle() to proceed even when no guess was locked in.
Remove the requirement that the current block is greater than the recorded guess block.
Query the blockhash of the current block instead of the recorded guess block.
Delete the state reset that clears the caller's guess block before evaluating the win condition.
Change the payout amount from 2 ether to 1 ether.
Reverse the winner check so the payout occurs when the stored guess does not match the answer.
Change the winner check to require a nonzero answer instead of allowing any nonzero answer while matching the guess.
Replace the inequality comparison in the winning condition with a strict less-than comparison, so the payout is sent when the guess does not match the answer.
Replace the inequality comparison in the winning condition with a strict greater-than comparison, so the payout is sent when the guess does not match the answer.
Replace the inequality comparison in the winning condition with a not-equal comparison against zero, so any nonzero guess wins regardless of the answer.
Replace the answer-validity guard with a check that answer equals zero, inverting when the payout can occur.
Replace the block-number strict inequality requirement with a non-strict greater-than-or-equal requirement, allowing settle in the same block as the recorded guess block.
Replace the payout amount with 1 ether, changing the value transferred after settle completes.
Replace the recorded block reset with a reset to the current block number, so future settle calls see a different block value.
